title: Cross-stream double-buffered I/O with KV-slab consolidation and NCCL QoS shaper
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes:
- Runtime: added optional cross-stream double-buffered host<->device I/O to reduce stalls during KV cache refills and large prefix handling.
- Runtime: consolidated small KV allocations into a slab allocator to cut allocation overhead and fragmentation.
- Scheduler: new NCCL QoS shaper to limit aggressive collective injection and prioritize latency-critical streams.
- Flags: enable_double_buf_io, kv_slab_size, nccl_qos_policy (see docs).
description:
Motivation: multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads are still sensitive to host↔device I/O stalls and small-KV allocation overheads. In heavy steady-state workloads the KV cache refills and occasional host-pageing cause tail latency spikes despite optimized kernels. This change introduces a coordinated cross-stream double-buffered I/O path together with a compact KV slab allocator and a lightweight NCCL traffic shaper (QoS) so that collectives from best-effort paths are rate-limited and latency-critical streams maintain priority.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Implement an explicit double-buffered transfer layer that runs producer/consumer queues on dedicated CUDA streams to overlap host pinned-memory staging and device memcpy with kernel launches; introduce a KV slab allocator that groups small KV items into pre-allocated slabs to avoid per-entry allocator overhead and reduce fragmentation; add a NCCL QoS shaper that tracks in-flight bytes per-peer and applies backpressure/spacing between large collective launches to avoid transient NIC saturation. Also wire runtime flags and observability hooks (per-stream token/byte counters and a dashboard gauge for QoS actions).

Key design points: The double-buffered I/O uses two pinned-worker buffers per GPU and a pair of CUDA streams: stream A handles transfers in while stream B feeds kernels; the buffers swap roles each microbatch. The slab allocator is a single owner-per-GPU arena with lock-free freelist for local threadpaths and a simple remote-return path for evictions. The NCCL shaper is opt-in and parameterized (bucket size, refill rate, priority masks). All features default to off to preserve existing behavior.

Benchmarks: microbench on 8x A100 (fp16) with a 32k context, continuous batching workload: p50 latency -2%, p95 -11%, p99 -18%; tokens/sec throughput +24% when enabled together compared to baseline with the same batcher. KV-heavy workload (large prefix reads) showed 35% fewer host-to-device memcpy stalls in tracing, and 3–6% lower allocation/GC CPU overhead in long-running runs.

Testing & safety: unit tests for slab allocator invariants and leak checks; synthetic multi-gpu integration test that flips enable_double_buf_io on/off under stress; CI perf job run (short) against a 4-GPU emulation reported stable improvements. Canary rollout plan: enable on 1% of infra, observe p99 and error budget for 48h; then ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback if p99 increases >5% or error rate >0.1%.

Migration and config: new runtime config keys (enable_double_buf_io, kv_slab_size_bytes, nccl_qos_policy). Defaults are conservative: double-buffering disabled, kv_slab_size 64MB, nccl_qos_policy "balanced". No API surface change.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of dbl-buffer I/O layer (runtime/comm/dbl_buffer.*) - [x] KV slab allocator (runtime/cache/kv_slab_*.cpp/.h) - [x] NCCL QoS shaper (runtime/scheduler/nccl_qos_*.cpp) - [x] Tests: unit + integration - [x] Bench scripts and dashboards updated - [x] Docs: runtime flags and rollback procedure added

Rollout notes: include monitoring on metrics runtime.io.dblbuf.swap_latency, runtime.kv.slab_util, scheduler.nccl.qos_throttle_count. If throttling events spike while target p99 worsens, disable QoS and investigate network counters.

Commits summary: see commits array for high-level messages.

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/comm/dbl_buffer.h and runtime/comm/dbl_buffer.cu: new double-buffer transfer layer and stream coordination. - runtime/cache/kv_slab_allocator.h/cpp: slab allocator for small KV entries with compacted freelist layout. - runtime/scheduler/nccl_qos_shaper.cpp: simple token-bucket shaper integrated at dispatch. - tests/integration/multi_gpu_kv_io_test.py: integration test that simulates heavy KV churn. - benchmarks/kv_slab_bench.py: microbench harness. - docs/runtime_flags.md: user-facing docs for flags and canary plan.

Related work and context: follows on design principles from prior comm scheduling PRs but aims to reduce host-device contention and allocation overhead rather than kernel fusion. This complements recent KV prefetch and async-kv work (see ENG-2145).

Repro steps for reviewers: run `pytest tests/integration/multi_gpu_kv_io_test.py -k dblbuf` on a 4+ GPU node; run benchmarks/kv_slab_bench.py with --iters 200 to reproduce throughput numbers.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Overall strong approach. A few nit picks: ensure the pinned buffer allocator falls back gracefully on systems without enough pinned memory and add metrics for buffer occupancy.
Aisha Khan (author): Added fallback to pageable buffers when pinned allocation fails and exported runtime.io.dblbuf.occupancy gauge. See commit a9d20ef for changes.

Marisol Vega: The NCCL shaper seems useful, but we should add a unit test that simulates rapid-fire collectives from two groups to ensure we don't deadlock. Also please document expected perf regression for best-effort workloads.
Aisha Khan (author): Added deadlock-simulation unit test and extended docs with best-effort notes. Adjusted default policy to "balanced" to avoid regressions.
Derek Liu: Can you add a small e2e canary playbook? Also ensure RBAC for toggling these flags in Private installs.
Aisha Khan (author): Canary playbook added to docs/runtime_flags.md; flag toggling uses existing admin-only endpoints in the private installer.
